name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
summary: Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus, ending imperial rule in the western Roman court.
details: In 476, Odoacer removed the teenage emperor Romulus Augustulus and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople. Western Roman administration did not vanish overnight, but the event became a powerful historical marker: the Latin west was now ruled by successor kingdoms, bishops, local aristocracies, and military leaders who adapted Roman systems to new political realities.
background: By the fifth century, the western Roman imperial office had become fragile, dependent on military strongmen and negotiated authority with Germanic federate leaders.
The deposition of Romulus Augustulus did not instantly erase Roman institutions, but it ended the line of western emperors recognized from Italy.
aftermath: Odoacer ruled Italy in the name of the eastern emperor, while western Europe continued to fragment into successor kingdoms that adapted Roman law, taxation, cities, and church structures.

paragraphs: Romulus Augustulus (last western emperor), Odoacer (Germanic chieftain who deposed him), and Zeno of Constantinople (eastern emperor who received the western imperial regalia).

paragraphs: Odoacer ruled Italy in the name of the eastern emperor, while western Europe continued to fragment into successor kingdoms that adapted Roman law, taxation, cities, and church structures.

contentSections.title: Historical significance
paragraphs: Fall of the Western Roman Empire matters because it reveals how medieval authority was made through conflict, ritual, writing, negotiation, and memory.
